status: EXTRACTED, NOT YET WIRED. Nothing reads this file. It records rulings that currently live only as evidence strings on detector rows, so that retiring a row cannot destroy them.
why_this_exists: Validation Source, S138: the detector was acting as an undocumented divergence registry. Every sloka id, translation divergence, commentary expansion and editorial reading lived in exactly one place -- an evidence string on a row. Retiring rows would have deleted the disagreements while the disagreements persisted.
binding_rule_PROPOSED_NOT_ACTIVE: Where this registry records a ruling, the ruling binds over the retrieved translation. NOT IMPLEMENTED: nothing carries a ruling into the interpreter prompt. Until it does, the interpreter follows the English, as capture 20260919T122618Z turn 2 shows.
oracle_discipline: JHora and AstroSage are GRADED-AGAINST, never DERIVED-FROM (P-027/P-028). One live breach is recorded under debts.oracle_supplied_condition.

unapplied_arm.why: Santhanam flags the 'in fall' arm as probably corrupt text in his own note; only the 11th arm is implemented.

ruling.english: R. Santhanam renders the subject as 'the 5th lord'.
ruling.sanskrit: The sloka reads sukha-sthaana-adhipa -- the lord of the 4th (sukha bhava).
ruling.ruling: SANSKRIT BINDS. v2 and v4 either side are both 4th-house rules; a 5th-lord rule between them is a non-sequitur.
ruling.live_conflict: CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION, capture 20260919T122618Z turn 2: the interpreter read the retrieved ENGLISH ('5th lord') and wrote 'not met here' into silent_on -- while the 5th lord (Mars) is Exalted, so under its own reading the condition WAS met. Detector and corpus disagree, and the interpreter followed the corpus.
ruling.unresolved: Nothing makes this ruling reach the interpreter at generation time. Wiring the registry into the payload is a separate, unbuilt change.

unapplied_arm.why: Needs degrees; the fact block carries none for this rule.

ruling.primary: The sloka states only an analogy: 'similarly consider Saturn and the 10th lord'. It names no placement.
ruling.expansion: The concrete placements (Saturn or the 10th lord in the 8th, with a malefic or the ascendant lord) come from R. Santhanam's note to the verse.
ruling.ruling: ADMITTED AS COMMENTARY, flagged in evidence. A reader may discount it.
ruling.basis: translator's note is not Parasara; it is the only operationalisation offered

unapplied_arm.why: Friendship tiers are deliberately out of the fact block as contested (S130). The rule UNDER-fires: a NOT-FIRED here does not mean the verse's condition failed.
No strength measure exists (Shadbala is not computed) and a dignity label was rejected as a proxy. The rule OVER-fires relative to the verse.

ruling.english: Renders Vajra as 'all benefics in the ascendant and the 7th OR all malefics in the 4th and 10th'.
ruling.ruling: BOTH ARMS REQUIRED, and all seven grahas confined to the angles.
ruling.basis: Read literally the OR fires on any chart with Jupiter and Venus angular, whatever the other five grahas do. No aakriti ('shape') yoga can mean that; every neighbouring verse in the family says 'all the planets'.
ruling.source_named: NONE -- this is an editorial reading, not a sourced one. Flagged per Validation Source.

ruling.text: 'None of these seven [sankhya] yogas will be operable, if another Nabhasa yoga explained earlier is derivable.'
ruling.conflict: The pre-existing _naabhasa_sankhya row fires unconditionally, contradicting its own chapter. Its verdict is asserted against the JHora oracle, so it was fenced rather than changed: a separate row naabhasa_sankhya_suppressed names the blockers.
ruling.needs: Sulabh's ruling -- two rows, or suppress the sankhya verdict directly. Validation Source notes the sankhya verdict is ungraded spec and the SOURCE should be fixed rather than fenced.

ruling.text: '3 angles occupied by benefics' (Maala) / by malefics (Sarpa).
ruling.taken: Three DISTINCT angles each holding at least one such graha; the fourth angle is not required to be vacant.
ruling.alternative: Exactly three, fourth vacant -- defensible and would change the verdict on real charts.

unapplied_arm.why: The maraka definition is not sourced from BPHS itself (P-028).

not_implemented.reason: Needs the ascendant lord 'bereft of strength'. No strength fact exists; a dignity label is not a strength proxy (P-032).
Needs the ascendant lord 'exceedingly strong'. Same missing fact.

Needs the 8th lord DEBILITATED IN THE ASCENDANT. Santhanam's own note to v12 shows this is unreachable by whole signs -- it needs a bhava cusp in an adjacent sign. A rule that can never fire is a false clean negative.

Chandra-Mangal yoga is Jataka Parijata / Phaladeepika, not BPHS. The corpus is BPHS-only, so a claim resting on it could cite no verse and the ghost guard would drop it. Out of corpus, not out of scope.

unsourced_rows.finding: 47 of 144 detector rows cite NO sloka. They were written from PVR's spec text or validated against the JHora oracle, and include the highest-value families in the system: every kendra-trikona raja link, all five Pancha Mahapurusha, all seven Neecha Bhanga, all three Vipareeta links, Gajakesari, Adhi, Vesi, Nipuna, Kalpadruma, Yogada and the sankhya Naabhasa set.
unsourced_rows.consequence: A predicate-redundancy admission test filters on decidability, not provenance -- so it would RETAIN all 47 unsourced rows while retiring 19 correctly-cited ones. The gate order is therefore source-named FIRST, predicate-redundancy SECOND.

oracle_supplied_condition.finding: An ambiguity in the PVR spec ('benefics occupy 6th, 7th AND 8th from the Moon' -- all three, or any?) was resolved by reading JHora's output for a reference chart. That is an ORACLE supplying a CONDITION.
oracle_supplied_condition.note: Recording it made it auditable; it did not cure it.
oracle_supplied_condition.required: Re-derive the reading from a spec source (BPHS ch37 v5 is in the corpus and states the same yoga), or demote the row to unsourced.
